title: CAGE: A FRAMEWORK FOR CULTURALLY ADAPTIVE RED-TEAMING BENCHMARK GENERATION

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of safety models on generic English prompts versus culturally-grounded, highly specific prompts (e.g., localized to Korean or Khmer contexts) to expose the 'Cultural Knowledge Gap' and English-centric safety alignment vulnerabilities.
Measuring the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of culturally-adapted red-teaming prompts designed to elicit age-based bias, discrimination, and hate speech, evaluated using an automated LLM-as-a-judge.

Measuring the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of culturally-adapted red-teaming prompts designed to elicit racial, ethnic, or color-based discrimination and hate speech, evaluated using an automated LLM-as-a-judge.
Measuring the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of culturally-adapted red-teaming prompts designed to elicit gender-based bias, discrimination, and hate speech, evaluated using an automated LLM-as-a-judge.
Measuring the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of culturally-adapted red-teaming prompts designed to elicit disability-based discrimination and hate speech, evaluated using an automated LLM-as-a-judge.

Measuring the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of culturally-adapted red-teaming prompts designed to elicit religion- or belief-based discrimination and hate speech, evaluated using an automated LLM-as-a-judge.

Measuring the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of culturally-adapted red-teaming prompts designed to elicit sexual orientation-based discrimination and hate speech, evaluated using an automated LLM-as-a-judge.

Measuring the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of culturally-adapted red-teaming prompts designed to elicit nationality- or geographic region-based prejudice (e.g., regional stereotypes in Korea), evaluated using an automated LLM-as-a-judge.
Measuring the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of culturally-adapted red-teaming prompts designed to elicit occupation-based discrimination and hate, evaluated using an automated LLM-as-a-judge.
